questions.question: From the collected samples of the following solutions from the science laboratory, the correct acid-base pair may be categorised as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**acetic acid (CH3COOH) and sodium hydroxide (NaOH)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An **acid-base pair** consists of one substance that acts as an **acid** (donates protons) and another that acts as a **base** (accepts protons or provides hydroxyl ions).
 
• **Sulphuric acid (H2SO4)** and **Nitric acid (HNO3)** are both **strong mineral acids**. Since both substances in this pair are **acids**, they do not form an acid-base category. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Acetic acid (CH3COOH)** is a **weak organic acid**, while **Sodium hydroxide (NaOH)** is a **strong base**. Together, they represent a valid **acid-base pair**. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• **Magnesium hydroxide [Mg(OH)2]** and **Ammonium hydroxide (NH4OH)** are both classified as **bases**. Because both chemicals possess **alkaline** properties, they do not constitute an acid-base pair. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Calcium hydroxide [Ca(OH)2]** and **Potassium hydroxide (KOH)** are both **strong bases** (metal hydroxides). This grouping consists of two **bases** rather than an acid and a base. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• In chemistry, identifying these pairs is fundamental for understanding **neutralization reactions** and **buffer solutions**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Acids**: These are substances that release **Hydrogen ions (H+)** when dissolved in water. They are known for their **sour taste** and their ability to turn **blue litmus paper red**. Common examples include **Hydrochloric acid (HCl)** and **Citric acid**.
 
• **Bases**: These substances release **Hydroxyl ions (OH-)** in aqueous solutions. They typically have a **bitter taste**, a **soapy/slippery feel**, and turn **red litmus paper blue**. Examples include **NaOH** and **Calcium carbonate**.
 
• **pH Scale**: The **acidity** or **alkalinity** of a solution is measured on the **pH scale**, which ranges from **0 to 14**. A **pH of 7** is neutral (like pure water), **below 7** is acidic, and **above 7** is basic or alkaline.
 
• **Neutralization**: This is a chemical reaction where an **acid** and a **base** react with each other to produce **salt and water**. For example, **CH3COOH** reacting with **NaOH** produces **Sodium Acetate (CH3COONa)** and **H2O**.
 
• **Strength of Acids/Bases**: **Strong acids** (like **H2SO4**) ionize completely in water, whereas **weak acids** (like **CH3COOH**) ionize only partially. Similarly, **NaOH** is a **strong base** compared to the **weak base NH4OH**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Acetic Acid (CH3COOH)**: Also known as **ethanoic acid**, it is the primary component of **vinegar**, usually making up about **4% to 8%** of the volume. It is widely used in the **food industry** as a preservative.
 
• **Sodium Hydroxide (NaOH)**: Commonly referred to as **caustic soda**, it is a highly **corrosive** base used in the manufacturing of **soaps, paper, and detergents**.
 
• **Arrhenius Theory**: This theory, proposed in **1884**, defines **acids** as substances that increase **H+** concentration and **bases** as substances that increase **OH-** concentration in water.
 
• **Indicators**: Chemical substances like **Phenolphthalein** and **Methyl Orange** are used to detect the presence of acids and bases. **Phenolphthalein** turns **pink** in a **basic** medium and remains **colorless** in an **acidic** medium.
 
• **Magnesium hydroxide [Mg(OH)2]**: Known as **Milk of Magnesia**, it is used medicinally as an **antacid** to treat indigestion by neutralizing excess **stomach acid**.

questions.question: Which type of compound is formed when sodium reacts with chlorine?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ionic compound**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An **Ionic compound** is formed when **Sodium (Na)** reacts with **Chlorine (Cl)**. This reaction results in the formation of **Sodium Chloride (NaCl)**, commonly known as **table salt**.
 
• **Sodium** is a metal belonging to **Group 1** of the periodic table with an **atomic number of 11**. It has **one electron** in its outermost shell and seeks to lose it to achieve a stable **octet configuration**.
 
• **Chlorine** is a non-metal belonging to **Group 17 (Halogens)** with an **atomic number of 17**. It has **seven electrons** in its valence shell and requires **one additional electron** to complete its octet.
 
• During the reaction, **Sodium** transfers its single valence electron to **Chlorine**. This complete transfer of electrons creates a **Sodium cation (Na+)** and a **Chloride anion (Cl-)**.
 
• The strong **electrostatic force of attraction** between these oppositely charged ions holds them together, forming an **Ionic Bond**. ***Hence, option 1 is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Covalent Compounds:**

 
 
• These are formed by the **sharing of electrons** between two or more **non-metals**.
 
• Examples include **Water (H2O)**, **Methane (CH4)**, and **Carbon Dioxide (CO2)**. Since Sodium is a metal and Chlorine is a non-metal, they do not form a covalent bond. ***Hence, option 2 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Coordinate (Dative) Compounds:**
 
 
• This is a type of covalent bond where **both electrons** in the shared pair come from the **same atom**.
 
• These are common in **complex ions** and **ammonium ions (NH4+)**. Sodium and Chlorine involve a complete transfer rather than a one-sided sharing. ***Hence, option 3 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Metallic Compounds:**
 
 
• These are formed through **metallic bonding**, which occurs between **metal atoms** where valence electrons are delocalized in a "**sea of electrons**."
 
• Examples include **Pure Iron (Fe)** or **Copper (Cu)**. Sodium Chloride is a salt, not a metallic alloy or pure metal. ***Hence, option 4 is incorrect.***
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Properties of NaCl:** **Sodium Chloride** forms a **crystalline lattice structure**. It has a **high melting point** of approximately **801 degrees Celsius** and a **high boiling point** of **1413 degrees Celsius**.
 
• **Electronegativity:** The **Pauling electronegativity** of **Sodium** is **0.93**, while **Chlorine** is **3.16**. The large difference of **2.23** (greater than **1.7**) confirms that the bond is predominantly **ionic**.
 
• **Conductivity:** As an **ionic compound**, **NaCl** does not conduct electricity in its **solid state** but is an excellent **conductor** when **molten** or **dissolved in water** due to the mobility of ions.
 
• **Solubility:** It is highly **soluble in polar solvents** like **Water** because the polar water molecules can stabilize the **Na+** and **Cl-** ions through **ion-dipole interactions**.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true about ligaments?

options.text: Ligaments are not highly flexible connective tissues connecting two bones.
Ligaments do not connect bones to bones and are very elastic.
Ligaments connect bones to bones and are very elastic with little matrix.
Ligaments connect muscles to bones and are highly flexible.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ligaments connect bones to bones and are very elastic with little matrix**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ligaments** are specialized types of **connective tissue** that serve the primary function of **connecting two bones** together at a joint.
 
• A key physical property of ligaments is that they are **highly elastic** and possess **great strength**, allowing for the necessary range of motion in the skeletal system while maintaining structural integrity. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• Unlike some other connective tissues, ligaments contain **very little matrix**, as they are primarily composed of densely packed **fibrous proteins**.
 
• **Ligaments** are flexible enough to allow movement but are strong enough to prevent **dislocation** of the joints. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect*** as it claims they are not flexible.
 
• By definition, their main role is **inter-bone connectivity**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect*** because it denies this connection.
 
• The task of connecting **muscles to bones** is performed by **tendons**, not ligaments. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Composition of Ligaments:**

 
 
• Ligaments are primarily made of **collagen fibers** and **elastin fibers**. While **collagen** provides **tensile strength** to withstand pressure, **elastin** provides the **flexibility** needed for movement.
 
• The cells found within ligaments are known as **fibroblasts**, which are responsible for the synthesis of the **extracellular matrix** and collagen.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Tendons:**
 
 
• While both are **fibrous connective tissues**, **tendons** are **tough** and **inelastic** compared to ligaments.
 
• **Tendons** anchor **skeletal muscles** to **bones**, facilitating the transmission of mechanical force required for movement.
 
 
 
• **Classification:**
 
 
• Ligaments are categorized under **Dense Regular Connective Tissue** because the collagen fibers are arranged in a **parallel pattern** to provide maximal resistance to pulling forces.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Clinical Significance:**

 
 
• An injury involving the **overstretching or tearing** of a ligament is medically termed a **sprain**. This is different from a **strain**, which involves muscles or tendons.
 
• Common examples of ligaments include the **Anterior Cruciate Ligament (ACL)** in the **knee**, which is vital for stabilizing the knee joint during rotational movements.
 
 
 
• **Functionality:**
 
 
• Ligaments act as **mechanical checks**; they limit the **range of motion** of a joint to protect it from moving in abnormal directions that could cause injury.
 
• They also contain **sensory nerve endings** (proprioceptors) that provide the brain with information regarding the **position and movement** of the joints.

questions.question: The discovery of which subatomic particle led to the development of Thomson's model?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Electron**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The discovery of the **electron** by **Sir J.J. Thomson** in **1897** was the primary catalyst for the development of the first modern atomic model.
 
• Thomson conducted experiments using a **Cathode Ray Tube (CRT)**, where he observed that rays were deflected away from a negatively charged plate and toward a positively charged plate, indicating they consisted of **negatively charged particles**.
 
• Following this discovery, **Thomson** proposed the **Plum Pudding Model** (also known as the **Watermelon Model**) in **1904** to explain the structure of the atom.
 
• In this model, the atom was envisioned as a **positively charged sphere** in which **negatively charged electrons** were embedded, similar to seeds in a watermelon or raisins in a pudding.
 
• This discovery was revolutionary because it proved that the atom was not an indivisible particle, as **John Dalton** had previously proposed in his **Atomic Theory**, but instead contained smaller **subatomic particles**.
 
• The model also established the concept of **electrical neutrality**, suggesting that the total positive charge of the sphere was exactly balanced by the total negative charge of the embedded electrons.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Proton**:

 
 
• While **Eugen Goldstein** observed **canal rays** (positive ions) in **1886**, the **proton** was identified as a fundamental subatomic particle by **Ernest Rutherford**.
 
• In **1919**, **Rutherford** proved that the nucleus of a hydrogen atom was present in other nuclei, leading to the naming of the **proton** in **1920**.
 
• The **proton** carries a **positive charge** of **+1.602 x 10^-19 Coulombs** and has a mass approximately **1836 times** that of an electron.
 
 
 
• **Neutron**:
 
 
• The **neutron** was discovered by **James Chadwick** in **1932**.
 
• He bombarded **Beryllium** with **alpha particles** and observed a new type of radiation that consisted of uncharged particles with a mass slightly greater than that of a proton.
 
• The discovery of the **neutron** explained why the atomic mass was often more than double the atomic number and helped in the understanding of **isotopes**.
 
 
 
• **Positron**:
 
 
• The **positron** is the **antiparticle** of the electron, discovered by **Carl D. Anderson** in **1932** while studying **cosmic rays**.
 
• It has the **same mass** as an electron but carries a **positive charge**. It was the first evidence of **antimatter**.
 
 
 
• **Rutherford’s Atomic Model**:
 
 
• Developed in **1911** following the **Alpha-particle Scattering Experiment** (Gold Foil Experiment).
 
• This model superseded Thomson's model by proposing that the atom has a tiny, dense, **positively charged nucleus** at its center, with electrons revolving around it, much like planets around the sun.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Chronology of Discovery**: The **electron** (1897) was discovered first, followed by the **proton** (identified in 1919), and finally the **neutron** (1932).
 
• **Charge-to-Mass Ratio**: J.J. Thomson is also famous for measuring the **charge-to-mass ratio (e/m)** of the electron, which he found to be constant regardless of the gas used in the discharge tube.
 
• **Nobel Prize**: **J.J. Thomson** was awarded the **Nobel Prize in Physics** in **1906** for his work on the conduction of electricity by gases and the discovery of the electron.

questions.question: If a current of 4 A flows through a resistor of 50 Omega for 8 minutes, the heat produced is _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**384 kJ**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The heat produced in a resistor when an electric current flows through it is governed by **Joule’s Law of Heating**. The formula used to calculate this heat energy (H) is **H = I²Rt**, where **I** is the current, **R** is the resistance, and **t** is the time duration.
 
• In the given problem, the value of the **current (I)** is **4 A** and the **resistance (R)** of the resistor is **50 Ω (ohms)**.
 
• The **time (t)** provided is **8 minutes**. Since the standard SI unit for time in physics calculations is seconds, we must convert it: **8 minutes = 8 × 60 = 480 seconds**.
 
• By substituting these values into the formula, we get **H = (4)² × 50 × 480**. This simplifies to **16 × 50 × 480**, which equals **384,000 Joules (J)**.
 
• To express the final answer in kilojoules (kJ), we divide the value by **1,000**. Therefore, **384,000 J / 1,000 = 384 kJ**. ***Hence, the correct answer is 384 kJ.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Joule's Law of Heating:**

 
 
• This law was formulated by the English physicist **James Prescott Joule** in the **1840s**. It states that the heat produced in a conductor is **directly proportional** to the **square of the current**, the **resistance** of the conductor, and the **time** for which the current flows.
 
• The mathematical expression is **H = I²Rt**. If the current is doubled, the heat produced increases by **four times**, assuming resistance and time remain constant.
 
 
 
• **Resistance (R):**
 
 
• Resistance is the property of a material to oppose the flow of electric current. Its SI unit is the **Ohm (Ω)**.
 
• In a resistor, the electrical energy lost due to collisions between electrons and the atoms of the conductor is converted into **thermal energy (heat)**.
 
 
 
• **Electric Power and Heat:**
 
 
• **Electric Power (P)** is the rate at which electrical energy is consumed or converted into other forms. It is given by **P = I²R** or **P = VI**.
 
• Heat energy can also be expressed as the product of **Power** and **Time** (**H = P × t**). In this case, the power dissipated is **800 Watts (W)**, and for **480 seconds**, the total energy is **384,000 J**.
 
 
 
• **Practical Applications of the Heating Effect:**
 
 
• **Domestic Appliances:** Devices such as **electric irons**, **electric heaters**, **geysers**, and **toasters** utilize high-resistance coils (often made of **Nichrome**) to generate significant heat.
 
• **Electric Bulbs:** The **filament** of an incandescent bulb (usually made of **Tungsten**) is heated to such a high temperature that it begins to emit light.
 
• **Electric Fuse:** A safety device consisting of a wire with a **low melting point**. When excessive current flows, the heat produced (**I²Rt**) melts the fuse wire, breaking the circuit and protecting appliances from damage.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Unit Conversions:** Always ensure that **time** is in **seconds** and **current** is in **Amperes** to get the energy in **Joules**. **1 kiloJoule (kJ)** is equivalent to **1,000 Joules (J)**.
 
• **Factors Affecting Heat:**
 
 
• If **Resistance** is increased, heat increases linearly.
 
• If **Current** is increased, heat increases exponentially (squared).
 
• If **Time** is increased, heat increases linearly.
 
 
 
• **Nature of the Energy:** The heat produced is a form of **waste energy** in many electronic circuits (like computers), requiring cooling systems like fans or **heat sinks**, but it is the primary desired output in heating appliances.

questions.question: The centre of curvature of a concave mirror is:

options.text: The midpoint of the mirror’s aperture
The point where parallel rays of light meet after reflection
The geometric centre of the spherical surface of which the mirror is a part
The point on the principal axis where image of an object at infinity is formed

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The geometric centre of the spherical surface of which the mirror is a part**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **reflecting surface** of a **spherical mirror** forms a part of a **sphere**. This sphere has a **centre**, and this point is called the **Centre of Curvature** of the spherical mirror.
 
• It is represented by the letter **C**. It is important to note that the **centre of curvature** is **not a part of the mirror**; it lies **outside** its reflecting surface.
 
• For a **concave mirror**, the **centre of curvature** lies in **front** of it. This point is the **geometric centre** of the **hollow sphere** of glass of which the mirror is a part. ***Hence, option 3 is correct.***
 
• The **midpoint** of the **mirror's aperture** or the **geometric centre** of the reflecting surface itself is called the **Pole (P)**, not the centre of curvature. ***Hence, option 1 is incorrect.***
 
• The point where **parallel rays** of light meet after reflection is the **Principal Focus (F)**. ***Hence, option 2 is incorrect.***
 
• The **image** of an **object at infinity** is formed at the **Principal Focus** of the mirror. ***Hence, option 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Radius of Curvature (R):** The **radius** of the **sphere** of which the reflecting surface of a spherical mirror forms a part is called the **Radius of Curvature**. It is the **distance** between the **Pole (P)** and the **Centre of Curvature (C)**.
 
• **Principal Axis:** An imaginary **straight line** passing through the **Pole** and the **Centre of Curvature** of a spherical mirror. It is **normal** to the mirror at its pole.
 
• **Principal Focus (F):** For a **concave mirror**, it is the point on the **principal axis** where all the **incident rays** that are **parallel** to the axis actually **converge** after reflection.
 
• **Focal Length (f):** The distance between the **Pole** and the **Principal Focus** of a spherical mirror is called the **focal length**. For mirrors with small **apertures**, the **radius of curvature** is found to be equal to **twice** the focal length (**R = 2f**).
 
• **Aperture:** The **diameter** of the reflecting surface of a spherical mirror is called its **aperture**. In elementary physics, we usually consider mirrors whose aperture is much **smaller** than its radius of curvature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Concave Mirror:** A **spherical mirror** whose **reflecting surface** is **curved inwards** (faces towards the centre of the sphere) is called a **concave mirror**. It is also known as a **converging mirror** because it converges light rays.
 
• **Convex Mirror:** A **spherical mirror** whose **reflecting surface** is **curved outwards** is called a **convex mirror**. The **centre of curvature** for a convex mirror lies **behind** the mirror. It is also known as a **diverging mirror**.
 
• **Light Path through C:** Any **ray of light** passing through the **centre of curvature** of a **concave mirror** (or directed in the direction of the centre of curvature of a convex mirror) is reflected back along the **same path** because the incident ray falls on the mirror along the **normal** to the reflecting surface.

questions.question: Why clove oil is used as an olfactory indicator?

options.text: Vigorous fuming of different colours is observed in acidic and basic medium.
Different colour effervescences are observed in acidic and basic medium.
It gives a different colour in acidic and basic medium.
It gives a different smell in acidic and basic medium.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It gives a different smell in acidic and basic medium.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Olfactory indicators** are substances whose **smell** or **odour** changes depending on whether they are placed in an **acidic** or **basic** medium.
 
• **Clove oil** is a classic example of an **olfactory indicator** used in chemistry laboratories to distinguish between **acids** and **bases**.
 
• When **clove oil** is added to an **acidic solution**, its characteristic **pungent smell** is **retained** and does not vanish.
 
• When **clove oil** is treated with a **basic solution**, such as **Sodium Hydroxide (NaOH)**, the characteristic **smell** of the oil is **lost** or cannot be detected.
 
• This property of changing **odour** based on the **pH** of the medium makes it a reliable tool for **chemical testing**. ***Hence, the correct answer is option 4.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Vanilla Essence**: Similar to **clove oil**, **vanilla essence** acts as an **olfactory indicator**. It maintains its pleasant **aroma** in **acidic** conditions but loses the **smell** when mixed with a **base**.
 
• **Onion**: Finely chopped **onions** can also be used as **olfactory indicators**. The **smell** of **onion** is destroyed when it reacts with a **basic solution**, whereas it persists in an **acidic solution**.
 
• **Utility for Visually Impaired**: **Olfactory indicators** are extremely important for **visually impaired students**, as they allow the identification of **acids** and **bases** through the sense of **smell** rather than relying on **colour** changes used in traditional indicators like **litmus** or **pH paper**.
 
• **Natural Indicators**: Apart from olfactory types, there are **natural indicators** like **litmus** (from **Lichens**), **Turmeric**, and **Red Cabbage** which change **colour** to indicate the nature of the substance.

• The main chemical component in **clove oil** responsible for its **odour** is **Eugenol**.
 
• In a **basic medium**, the **hydroxide ions** react with the **acidic** functional groups of the indicator molecules (like **Eugenol**), changing their **chemical structure** and consequently neutralizing the **scent**.
 
• **Acids** have a **pH** less than **7**, while **bases** have a **pH** greater than **7**.
 
• The **fuming** or **effervescence** mentioned in other options usually relates to reactions involving **carbonates** (releasing **CO2**) or strong **oxidizing agents**, rather than the standard behavior of an **olfactory indicator**.
 
• Testing for **acids** and **bases** using **smell** is a qualitative analysis technique that provides immediate results without the need for complex electronic equipment.

questions.question: Two resistors, R₁ ​ and R2 , are connected in parallel. Their equivalent resistance is 5 Omega . When one of them is removed, the resistance of the circuit increases to 10 Omega . Which of the following is the correct value of the other resistor?

• The mathematical formula for two resistors (**R1** and **R2**) in parallel is: **1/Req = 1/R1 + 1/R2**.
 
• According to the question, the **equivalent resistance** of the two resistors in parallel is **5 Ω**.

অত্যাধিক অনুৰণনৰ ফলত কথা-বতৰাত ব্যাঘাত হ'ব পাৰে।
কঠিন দেৱাল থকা ডাঙৰ হলবোৰত অনুৰণন সাধাৰণ।
শব্দৰ পুনঃ পুনঃ প্ৰতিফলনৰ ফলত অনুৰণন হয়।

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**অনুৰণনে শব্দৰ স্পষ্টতা উন্নত কৰাত সহায় কৰে।**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **শব্দৰ অনুৰণন (Reverberation)** হ’ল শব্দৰ উৎসটো বন্ধ হোৱাৰ পিছতো শব্দটো কিছু সময়ৰ বাবে ৰৈ যোৱা পৰিঘটনা। ই শব্দৰ **পুনঃ পুনঃ প্ৰতিফলনৰ (Multiple Reflection)** ফলত সংঘটিত হয়। *গতিকে, চতুৰ্থ বিবৃতিটো (৪) শুদ্ধ।*
 
• যেতিয়া শব্দটো **কঠিন দেৱাল (Hard walls)** থকা এটা **ডাঙৰ হলত (Large Hall)** উৎপন্ন হয়, তেতিয়া ই দেৱাল, চিলিং আৰু মজিয়াৰ পৰা বাৰে বাৰে প্ৰতিফলিত হয়, যাৰ ফলত শব্দটো দীৰ্ঘ সময় ধৰি শুনা যায়। *গতিকে, তৃতীয় বিবৃতিটো (৩) শুদ্ধ।*
 
• অত্যাধিক অনুৰণনৰ ফলত এটা শব্দ শেষ হোৱাৰ আগতেই আন এটা শব্দ আৰম্ভ হয়, যাৰ ফলত শব্দবোৰ এটাৰ ওপৰত আনটো সোমাই পৰে। ইয়াৰ ফলত শব্দৰ স্পষ্টতা হ্ৰাস পায় আৰু **কথা-বতৰাত ব্যাঘাত (Disruption in conversation)** জন্মে। *গতিকে, দ্বিতীয় বিবৃতিটো (২) শুদ্ধ।*
 
• অনুৰণনে শব্দৰ স্পষ্টতা উন্নত কৰাত সহায় নকৰে, বৰঞ্চ ই শব্দটোক **অস্পষ্ট (Blurred)** কৰি তোলে। এক নিৰ্দিষ্ট সীমাৰ ওপৰত অনুৰণন হ’লে কথা বা সংগীত বুজাত অসুবিধা হয়। *গতিকে, প্ৰথম বিবৃতিটো (১) অশুদ্ধ বা শুদ্ধ নহয়।*
 
• ***গতিকে, শুদ্ধ উত্তৰটো হ’ল ১।***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **অনুৰণন কাল (Reverberation Time):** শব্দৰ উৎসটো বন্ধ হোৱাৰ পিছত শব্দৰ তীব্ৰতা **৬০ ডেচিবল (60 dB)** লৈ হ্ৰাস পাবলৈ যিমান সময়ৰ প্ৰয়োজন হয়, তাক অনুৰণন কাল বুলি কোৱা হয়। এটা আদর্শ হলঘৰৰ বাবে এই সময় অতি বেছিও হ’ব নালাগে আৰু অতি কমো হ’ব নালাগে।
 
• **শব্দ শোষক সামগ্ৰী (Sound Absorbent Materials):** ডাঙৰ প্ৰেক্ষাগৃহ বা চিনেমা হলত অনুৰণন নিয়ন্ত্ৰণ কৰিবলৈ **কম্প্ৰেছড্ ফাইবারবোর্ড (Compressed fibreboard)**, **পৰ্দা (Curtains)**, **গালিচা (Carpets)** আৰু **অকৌষ্টিক টাইলছ (Acoustic tiles)** ব্যৱহাৰ কৰা হয়। এইবোৰে শব্দ প্ৰতিফলিত কৰাৰ পৰিবৰ্তে **শোষণ (Absorption)** কৰি লয়।
 
• **প্ৰতিধ্বনি (Echo) বুলি কি বুজা যায়:** যেতিয়া এটা শব্দ কোনো বাধাৰ পৰা প্ৰতিফলিত হৈ পুনৰ আমাৰ কাণলৈ আহে, তাক প্ৰতিধ্বনি বোলে। প্ৰতিধ্বনি স্পষ্টকৈ শুনিবলৈ উৎস আৰু বাধাৰ মাজৰ দূৰত্ব কমেও **১৭.২ মিটাৰ** হোৱা উচিত।
 
• **ব্যৱহাৰিক উদাহৰণ:** চিনেমা হলত অনুৰণনৰ বাবেই শব্দটো গম্ভীৰ আৰু শক্তিশালী যেন লাগে, কিন্তু ইয়াক সঠিকভাৱে নিয়ন্ত্ৰণ কৰিবলৈ দেৱালবোৰত শব্দ শোষক কাপোৰ বা বোৰ্ড লগোৱা থাকে যাতে কথাৰ স্পষ্টতা হেৰাই নাযায়।

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **শব্দৰ প্ৰতিফলনৰ সূত্ৰ:** পোহৰৰ দৰে শব্দৰ প্ৰতিফলনৰ ক্ষেত্ৰতো **আপতন কোণ (Angle of Incidence)** আৰু **প্ৰতিফলন কোণ (Angle of Reflection)** সমান হয়।
 
• **উচ্চ অনুৰণনৰ কুফল:** বিদ্যালয়ৰ শ্ৰেণীকোঠা বা সভাঘৰত বেছি অনুৰণন হ’লে বক্তাৰ কথা **অস্পষ্ট** হৈ পৰে, যাক **Acoustically poor** বুলি কোৱা হয়।
 
• **আর্কিটেকচাৰেল ডিজাইন:** আধুনিক স্থাপত্যবিদসকলে প্ৰেক্ষাগৃহ নিৰ্মাণ কৰোঁতে শব্দ বিজ্ঞানৰ **(Acoustics)** নীতি অনুসৰণ কৰে যাতে অনুৰণন আৰু প্ৰতিধ্বনি সঠিক ভাৱে নিয়ন্ত্ৰণ কৰিব পাৰি।

questions.question: Which of the following is parenchyma type and present in aquatic plants, with large air cavities to help them float?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Aerenchyma**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Aerenchyma** is a specialized type of **parenchyma** tissue characterized by the presence of **large air cavities** or intercellular spaces.
 
• It is primarily found in **aquatic plants** (also known as **hydrophytes**), such as **Lotus**, **Water Hyacinth (Eichhornia)**, and **Hydrilla**.
 
• The main function of these air cavities is to provide **buoyancy** to the plant, which helps them **float** on or near the water surface. ***Hence, option 2 is correct.***
 
• Beyond buoyancy, **aerenchyma** also facilitates the **internal diffusion of gases** like **oxygen** and **carbon dioxide** between the aerial parts and the submerged tissues, which is vital for **respiration** and **photosynthesis** in an aquatic environment.
 
• The cells in this tissue are typically thin-walled and arranged in a way that creates a **sponge-like** network within the **cortex** of roots and stems.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Chlorenchyma**: 
 
 
• This is a type of **parenchyma** that contains **chlorophyll** and is responsible for performing **photosynthesis**.
 
• It is commonly found in the **mesophyll** of **leaves** and the outer green layers of **herbaceous stems**. ***Hence, option 1 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Tracheid**: 
 
 
• **Tracheids** are elongated, tube-like cells that form a part of the **xylem** (complex permanent tissue).
 
• These cells are **dead at maturity**, have **lignified** walls, and are responsible for the **conduction of water** and minerals in vascular plants. ***Hence, option 3 is incorrect.***

__
 
• **Gregor Johann Mendel**, during his pioneering inheritance studies in the **mid-19th century**, proposed that every trait in a sexually reproducing organism is controlled by **two** copies of a discrete unit called a **factor**.
 
• These **factors**, which we now identify as **genes**, are passed from parents to offspring. Mendel suggested that an individual receives **one** factor from each parent, resulting in a pair that determines the expressed characteristic.
 
• This concept was fundamental to his **Law of Segregation**, which states that during the formation of gametes (eggs and sperm), the **two** copies of each factor separate so that each gamete carries only **one** factor for each trait.
 
• Upon fertilization, the **two** factors are restored in the zygote, ensuring that the offspring has a complete set of **two** factors, maintaining the **diploid** nature of the organism.
 
• The presence of **two** copies allows for variations in traits, as the factors can be identical (**homozygous**) or different (**heterozygous**).

• **Pisum sativum (Garden Pea):** Mendel chose the **garden pea** for his experiments conducted between **1856** and **1863**. This plant was ideal because it had **seven** distinct pairs of contrasting traits, such as **tall vs. dwarf** stems and **round vs. wrinkled** seeds.
 
• **Alleles:** In modern genetics, the different forms of a **factor** are called **alleles**. For example, the gene for height has two alleles: **T** (tall) and **t** (dwarf).
 
• **Dominant and Recessive:** Mendel observed that in a pair of different factors, one could mask the expression of the other. The expressed factor is **dominant**, while the masked one is **recessive**.
 
• **Genotype vs. Phenotype:** The **genotype** refers to the actual genetic makeup (the **two** factors/alleles present, e.g., **Tt**), whereas the **phenotype** is the observable physical characteristic (e.g., a **tall** plant).
 
• **Monohybrid Cross:** By crossing plants with **two** different versions of a single trait, Mendel consistently observed a **3:1 ratio** in the **F2 generation**, which statistically proved the existence of paired factors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Publication and Rediscovery:** Mendel published his findings in **1866** in the paper "Experiments on Plant Hybridization." However, his work remained largely ignored until its rediscovery in **1900** by **Hugo de Vries**, **Carl Correns**, and **Erich von Tschermak**.
 
• **Diploidy:** The proposal of **two** factors aligns with the biological reality of **homologous chromosomes**. Humans and many other organisms are **diploid**, meaning they have **two** sets of chromosomes, one from each parent.
 
• **Mendel’s Laws:** His studies led to the formulation of three major laws: the **Law of Dominance**, the **Law of Segregation**, and the **Law of Independent Assortment**.
 
• **Significance:** The realization that **two** copies of a factor control inheritance provided the mathematical basis for the science of **genetics**, allowing scientists to predict the probability of traits appearing in future generations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

• **Acceleration** is defined as the **rate of change of velocity** of an object with respect to **time**. It describes how quickly the speed or direction of a moving body changes.

• The formula for **acceleration (a)** is derived from the change in velocity divided by the time interval: **a = (Final Velocity - Initial Velocity) / Time**. ***Hence, the statement a = (v - u) / t is correct.***
 
• If an object moves with **constant velocity**, the **acceleration** is **zero** because the difference between the final and initial velocity (v - u) is null.
 
• **Acceleration** is a **vector quantity**, meaning it possesses both **magnitude** and **direction**. It points in the same direction as the change in velocity.

• In terms of dimensional analysis, it is represented as **[M⁰ L¹ T⁻²]**.
 
 
 
• **Equations of Motion:**

• The **Reactivity Series** of metals, also known as the **Activity Series**, is an arrangement of metals in the descending order of their **chemical reactivity**. It helps in predicting the outcome of displacement reactions and the extraction methods for metals.
 
• **Potassium (K)** is an **Alkali metal** belonging to **Group 1** of the periodic table. It is highly electropositive and is one of the most reactive metals, reacting vigorously with **water** and **air**. It occupies a position at the very top of the reactivity series.
 
• **Magnesium (Mg)** is an **Alkaline earth metal** in **Group 2**. While it is highly reactive, its ability to lose **electrons** is lower than that of Group 1 metals like Potassium. It reacts slowly with cold water but rapidly with **boiling water** or **steam**.
 
• **Aluminium (Al)** belongs to **Group 13**. It is less reactive than Magnesium. Although it is quite reactive, it often forms a thin, protective layer of **Aluminium Oxide** on its surface, which prevents further reaction. In the series, it follows Magnesium.
 
• **Zinc (Zn)** is a **Transition metal**. It is less reactive than Aluminium and Magnesium. It does not react with cold water but reacts with **steam** to form zinc oxide and hydrogen gas.
 
• Based on the tendency of these metals to lose electrons and form **positive ions**, the correct decreasing order of reactivity is **Potassium (K)** > **Magnesium (Mg)** > **Aluminium (Al)** > **Zinc (Zn)**. ***Hence, the correct answer is K > Mg > Al > Zn.***

• Conversely, **Zinc** cannot displace **Magnesium** from its salt solution because it is lower in the series.
 
 
 
• **Reaction with Acids**:
 
 
• Metals placed above **Hydrogen** in the reactivity series (like K, Mg, Al, and Zn) can displace **Hydrogen gas** from dilute **hydrochloric acid** or **sulphuric acid**.
 
• The rate of evolution of hydrogen bubbles decreases as we move from **Potassium** to **Zinc** in the series.
 
 
 
• **Periodic Table Trends**:
 
 
• In the periodic table, **metallic character** (reactivity) generally **increases** as we go **down a group** due to increasing atomic size and decreasing **ionization energy**.
 
• Reactivity generally **decreases** across a period from **left to right** as the **effective nuclear charge** increases, making it harder for atoms to lose electrons.

• **Storage of Potassium**: Due to its extreme reactivity with **oxygen** and **moisture** in the air, **Potassium (K)** and **Sodium (Na)** are always stored under **Kerosene** to prevent accidental fires.
 
• **Galvanization**: **Zinc (Zn)** is used in the process of **Galvanization**. Since Zinc is more reactive than **Iron (Fe)**, it acts as a sacrificial layer, corroding first and protecting the underlying iron from **rusting**.
 
• **Reduction Methods**:
 
 
• High-reactivity metals (K, Na, Ca, Mg, Al) are extracted via **Electrolytic Reduction** of their molten chlorides or oxides.
 
• Medium-reactivity metals (Zn, Fe, Pb) are usually extracted by **reducing** their oxides with **Carbon (Coke)**.
 
 
 
• **Amphoteric Nature**: Both **Aluminium** and **Zinc** are special because they react with both **acids** and **bases** to produce hydrogen gas, showing **amphoteric** properties.
